children: Anmol Industries IPO plans include a Rs 1,800 crore offer for sale as the Kolkata-based biscuit maker files draft papers with SEBI

Biscuit and bakery products maker Anmol Industries has filed draft papers with the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) for an initial public offering of up to Rs 1,800 crore, according to the draft documents.

The proposed issue will comprise entirely an offer for sale (OFS), with no fresh issue of shares. The Baijnath Choudhary & Family Trust, which holds around 84 per cent of Anmol Industries, will be the sole selling shareholder. As a result, the company will not receive any proceeds from the IPO.

Anmol Industries reported a sharp improvement in financial performance in the year ended March 31, with net profit rising five-fold to Rs 191 crore. Revenue increased 28 per cent to around Rs 2,100 crore during the year. Founded in 1994, the Kolkata-based company manufactures and sells biscuits, cookies and cakes across its portfolio of around 70 brands. It also exports its products to 31 countries. The company competes with listed packaged-food companies including Britannia Industries, ITC and Mrs Bectors Food Specialities.

The proposed IPO marks Anmol Industries’ second attempt to access the public markets. The company had received SEBI approval for a Rs 750 crore IPO in 2018 but did not proceed with the listing. Intensive Fiscal Services, ICICI Securities and IIFL Capital Services have been appointed as the book-running lead managers for the proposed issue. The latest filing comes amid renewed activity in India’s primary market following a relatively muted first half of 2026.

The IPO will provide the promoter trust with an opportunity to sell part or all of its holding, while the absence of a fresh issue means the transaction will not bring new equity capital into Anmol Industries.
